Avalanche Risk Modelling — Valais, Switzerland

The challenge

The authorities of the Valais canton needed a GIS-based analysis to prioritise towns and villages for avalanche risk mitigation measures. The challenge was to turn terrain conditions and population exposure into a single ranked figure per settlement that could directly inform where mitigation budget goes first.

Basemap

A cell is high risk where all three conditions hold: elevation ≥ 1500 m, slope 35–40°, and aspect facing NW–N–E (293°–113°). Each settlement's risk index is the count of high-risk cells inside a population-scaled buffer, ln(pop) × 200 m. Grid 200 m, modelled in EPSG:21781 (CH1903 / LV03).

Loading map…
Toggle the model layers on or off, drag the slider to fade the relief, click any settlement for its figures, or pick one from the most-exposed list to fly there. The approach

A 200 m digital elevation model of the canton was used to derive slope and aspect, and the three terrain criteria known to produce slab avalanches were intersected into a single boolean surface — elevation at or above 1500 m, slope between 35° and 40°, and a north-facing aspect from NW through N to E. Each of the 118 settlements was then buffered by a radius scaled to its population, ln(pop) × 200 m, and the high-risk cells falling inside that buffer were counted with zonal statistics. That count became the settlement's risk index, giving the canton a single ranked list to work down.

Key outcomes

192.4 km² of terrain flagged as high risk — 3.69% of the canton, across 4 810 cells

44 of 118 settlements carry measurable exposure and are ranked for mitigation priority

Terrain criteria combined with population-scaled buffers to weight risk by who it affects
